title: 3. What Really Happened
description: Chapter 3 of 3 of “The Case of the Missing Star”. Read in order.

cover.alt: The Case of the Missing Star

illustration.alt: They uncover the star, examine the evidence, and test the loose bow.

lines: Luna and Nico lift the striped cloth completely away.
There is the star, with its purple ring and the dotted ribbon trailing towards one of the cart's wheels.
blocks.title: There it is!

lines: The decoration is undamaged.
Luna notices the undone bow and the small torn edge of ribbon;
their explanation will need to account for those details too.
blocks.title: Whole, but loose

lines: They place the star and ribbon beside the cart to bring the evidence together.
Finding the object answers where it was, but not how it arrived.
blocks.title: Putting it together

lines: Luna gently pulls one end of the loose bow and watches it open.
The test shows it could come free without cutting the ribbon or breaking the ring.
blocks.title: Testing the bow

variants.retryFeedback: Watch what happens when the ribbon end is pulled.

variants.prompt: What does testing the loose bow show?

options.text: It could open when one end was pulled

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! It could open when one end was pulled.
variants.retryFeedback: Watch what happens when the ribbon end is pulled.

illustration.alt: Reconstruction: wind loosens the bow, the star falls and is covered, and the cart leaves traces.

lines: The story returns to the moment before the disappearance.
Wind shook the flags and ribbon while the cart passed directly beneath the star on its hook.
blocks.title: The wind returns

lines: The bow finally slipped open, dropping the star onto the cloth inside the cart.
Pico was looking ahead, so he did not see what happened behind him.
blocks.title: Falls into the cart

lines: As the decoration landed, a loose fold of cloth flipped over it.
The star remained whole inside the cart, even though nobody could see it from outside.
blocks.title: Covered by the cloth

lines: The wheels left long lines in the mud.
A trailing ribbon end caught beside the path, tearing off the small scrap the children would discover later.
blocks.title: The ribbon catches

variants.prompt: What hid the star inside the cart?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! A fold of cloth.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow this page’s four pictures in order.

options.text: The cloth moves, the cat ties the star, then wind arrives
The bow opens, the star falls, and the cloth covers it
The cart empties, the star flies up, and the bow tightens

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! The bow opens, the star falls, and the cloth covers it.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow this page’s four pictures in order.

illustration.alt: They return the star, tie a double knot, test it, and enjoy the party.

lines: Back in the present, they return the star to its hook.
A fall and a ride explain the clues without needing to imagine that somebody stole it.
blocks.title: Back to the hook

lines: Luna ties a double knot while Nico holds the decoration steady.
Understanding what failed lets them change the fastening instead of simply hanging it the same way.
blocks.title: A double knot

lines: They test the knot with a gentle tug and watch it stay firm.
Looking secure is not enough; they check whether their repair actually works this time.
blocks.title: Testing it holds

lines: The party begins with the star in place.
The children have learned that a good explanation must fit the evidence, even when it challenges their first suspicion.
blocks.title: The party begins!

variants.prompt: How does Luna fasten the star more securely?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! With a double knot.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the knot and what they do before the party starts.

variants.prompt: Why do they give the star a gentle tug at the end?

options.text: To check that their repair works

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! To check that their repair works.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the knot and what they do before the party starts.

ribbon.definition: A narrow strip of fabric used for tying or decorating.
ribbon.example: She tied a red ribbon around the gift before giving it away.

bow.definition: A knot with loops that can be loosened by pulling an end.
bow.example: He tied a bow on his shoelaces so they wouldn't come undone.

hook.definition: A curved piece used to hang something.
hook.example: We hung the keys on a hook by the door.

evidence.definition: Information used to check an explanation.
evidence.example: She kept the photo as evidence that she arrived first.

scrap.definition: A small piece left or torn from something.
scrap.example: He used a scrap of fabric to patch the torn backpack.

explanation.definition: An account of how or why something happened.
explanation.example: She gave a simple explanation for why she was late.

decoration.definition: Something used to make a place look special.
decoration.example: We hung paper decorations around the classroom for the party.

suspicion.definition: An idea that might be true but needs checking.
suspicion.example: He had a suspicion that someone had borrowed his pencil without asking.

undamaged.example: The package arrived undamaged after the long trip.

fastening.definition: A way of holding something in place.
fastening.example: The fastening on her backpack kept it from opening by accident.
